subject: Cleanroom viewer proposal — secure PT exchange & exec summary redaction
messages:
From: Claire O'Reilly <claire.oreilly@nimbussec.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: John Patel <john.patel@acmecloud.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: pen-test report access and exec summary

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Procurement at Acme (cc'd) is asking for the latest penetration test report and the executive summary so they can close the vendor security review. A few constraints from their side:

- The report needs to be available to security and procurement but must not be downloadable outside a controlled viewer.
- Any customer-specific IP addresses or internal hostnames should be redacted from the version shared with procurement; security will want the full version under an NDA.
- We need a statement of remediation status for high/critical findings (open vs closed) and dates.

Can Redwood provide a secure viewing option (time-limited, watermarked) and a proposed redaction matrix? If possible, we'd like to have an exec summary we can share by EOD Tuesday (21 Oct).

Regards,
Claire
Senior Security Manager
Nimbus Security

--
Nimbus Security (external vendor)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire O'Reilly <claire.oreilly@nimbussec.com>
Cc: John Patel <john.patel@acmecloud.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Oct 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: pen-test report access and exec summary

Hi Claire —

Appreciate the clear asks. Short answer: yes. Proposed exchange model below so procurement gets what they need without exposing raw evidence.

1) Cleanroom viewer (recommended): we will upload the full report and supporting evidence to a secure, ephemeral viewer (read-only, watermark by viewer identity, no downloads/prints). Viewer access will be time-limited (default 7 days) and tied to authenticated emails.

2) Executive summary (redacted): we will produce a redacted exec summary (PII/hostnames/IoCs removed) that Acme procurement can download. We will attach a redaction matrix describing each removed artifact and the rationale.

3) Full report under NDA: security reviewers can request the full report; we will require a signed mutual NDA (or a redline of Redwood's standard addendum). Once returned, we can provide cleanroom access to the unredacted material for named reviewers only.

4) Remediation status: we'll include a remediation table mapping each finding to status, owner, and target close date. We can also provide a short summary of mitigations for critical items.

Timeline suggestions:
- Today: send proposed redaction matrix and cleanroom instructions.
- Mon Oct 20: deliver draft redacted exec summary for Acme procurement review.
- Tue Oct 21: finalize and deliver exec summary after procurement feedback.

Kimberly and Marissa from my team are looped in to handle legal/redaction work and evidence packaging. Any hard constraints (legal wording or commodity controls) from your side that would prevent watermarking or viewer access? Also — is DocuSign acceptable for the NDA?

I'll attach a short instructions stub and the redaction template now.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0218

Attachments: cleanroom_access_instructions.txt, redaction_matrix_v1.xlsx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire O'Reilly <claire.oreilly@nimbussec.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Oct 2025 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: pen-test report access and exec summary — redaction scope

Claire / Jordan —

Thanks — a few legal/controls clarifications from Redwood's side:

- We can provide a redacted exec summary for procurement and a sealed, full report to named technical reviewers. The cleanroom viewer is our preferred control because it minimizes copies and supports watermarking and session logs.

- Redaction carveouts: we do not redact Indicators of Compromise (IoCs) that are vendor-introduced or generic (e.g., "suspicious domain xyz[.]com") where redaction would impede remediation. We will, however, redact customer-unique internal hostnames and IPs in the procurement-facing document.

- Evidence access: for third-party auditors we require an NDA and either an identity-verified session or an HHR (hardware-held review) for air-gapped customers.

- DocuSign is fine for NDAs. Please use the following link for our standard PT share addendum: https://app.docusign.com/Envelope/ABC-123-PT-SHARE (signature by both parties). Once signed we will enable the unredacted viewer session for named accounts.

I'll prepare a redaction matrix indicating which sections will be blanked/obfuscated and include suggested remediation status language (Open / In progress / Fixed — with dates). Marissa will own the packaging and access controls.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Security & Privacy | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com

--
Redwood Inference (internal)

From: Claire O'Reilly <claire.oreilly@nimbussec.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: John Patel <john.patel@acmecloud.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Oct 2025 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: pen-test report access and exec summary

Jordan / Kimberly —

Thanks, that model sounds good. A couple of quick follow-ups from procurement and security:

- Procurement wants the redacted exec summary to be downloadable (PDF) and stamped with a company watermark. That is acceptable if the viewer clearly indicates the redactions and the matrix is attached.
- Security (me) will sign the DocuSign addendum for unredacted access; can you confirm whether we can request a short-term export of evidence (logs) for our internal tracker? If not, the session logs from your cleanroom will likely suffice.
- Procurement also asked whether Redwood offers a one-time onboarding credit or demo credit if we proceed to production by Nov 30 — they said it'd speed approvals.

We can sign the DocuSign today once you confirm the final redaction rules for hostnames/IPs and whether IoCs will be present in the sealed report.

—Claire

--
Nimbus Security (external)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire O'Reilly <claire.oreilly@nimbussec.com>, John Patel <john.patel@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Oct 2025 16:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: pen-test report access and exec summary — next steps

Claire / John —

Confirmed next steps from Redwood:

1) Kimberly attached (sent privately to Claire) a redaction matrix outlining hostnames/IPs that will be redacted for procurement and the IoC policy for the sealed report.
2) Marissa will upload the sealed report into the cleanroom and provision time-limited access once the DocuSign addendum is signed.
3) I'm attaching the draft redacted exec summary (redwood_pt_execsum_redacted_v1.pdf) and the redaction matrix; procurement-facing PDF includes our watermark and an explanatory footnote referencing the matrix.
4) On credits: we can offer a one-time onboarding credit (pricing team approved) that procurement can apply if they sign and deploy by Nov 30; I'll follow up with a short pricing note.

Please sign the DocuSign at https://app.docusign.com/Envelope/ABC-123-PT-SHARE and reply with the list of reviewer emails you want provisioned for the cleanroom.

Thanks — I'll track this as a MAM (mutual action plan) and follow up with a calendar invite for the review window.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: redwood_pt_execsum_redacted_v1.pdf, redaction_matrix_v1.xlsx

--
Internal note: Marissa, please stage the cleanroom upload after DocuSign executes and set access TTL to 7 days. Kimberly, confirm final redaction matrix version (v1 -> v1.1) before we enable procurement download.
